import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a visually appealing theme for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Megapixels and Price

sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',        # Color points by brand
    style='body_type',  # Use different marker styles for body types
    s=250,              # Set a fixed size for the markers for better visibility
    palette='deep',     # Choose a distinct color palette
    legend='full'       # Ensure all legend elements are shown
)

# Annotate each point with its 'model_year' for additional context.
# This is particularly useful for a small dataset to highlight individual data points.
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(
        row['megapixels'] + 0.7, # X-coordinate offset for text
        row['price_usd'] + 70,   # Y-coordinate offset for text
        f"'{str(row['model_year'])[2:]}", # Display last two digits of the year
        horizontalalignment='left',
        verticalalignment='bottom',
        fontsize=9,
        color='dimgray',
        weight='semibold'
    )

# Add informative title and axis labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Brand and Body Type (Model Year Annotated)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Adjust the legend position to avoid overlapping with the plot area
plt.legend(title='Camera Details', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')
